tools.name: read_pcblib
tools.title: Read a PcbLib
tools.description: Read an Altium .PcbLib file and return its contents including footprints with their primitives (pads, vias, tracks, arcs, regions, fills, text, component_bodies). Returns structured data that can be used to understand existing footprint styles. All coordinates and dimensions are in millimetres (mm). Fields such as guid, unique_id, raw_tail, raw_block, raw_geometry, raw_layer_id, param_key_order and primitive_order are fidelity carriers: pass them back unchanged to write_pcblib or update_component and the rewrite is byte-identical to the source; omit them when authoring from scratch. Each footprint is the same JSON shape get_component, export_library and write_pcblib use; a list with no entries and an optional field with no value are omitted rather than empty/null. For large libraries, use component_name to fetch specific footprints, or use limit/offset for pagination.

compact.description: If true (default), omit per-layer pad data when stack_mode is Simple. Set to false for full output.

component_name.description: Optional: fetch only this footprint, by name in any case; a name the library does not hold is an error naming the available footprints

filepath.description: Path to the .PcbLib file

limit.description: Optional: maximum number of footprints to return, 1 or more (default: all)

offset.description: Optional: skip the first N footprints, 0 or more (default: 0)

tools.name: read_schlib
tools.title: Read a SchLib
tools.description: Read an Altium .SchLib file and return its contents including symbols with their primitives (pins, rectangles, round_rects, lines, polylines, polygons, arcs, pies, images, text_frames, beziers, ellipses, elliptical_arcs, labels, ieee_symbols), parameters and footprint links. Coordinates are in schematic units (10 units = 1 grid square, not mm). Fields such as unique_id, primitive_order, header_params, raw_params, all_pin_count and extra_streams are fidelity carriers: pass them back unchanged to write_schlib or update_component and the rewrite is byte-identical to the source; omit them when authoring from scratch. Each symbol is the same JSON shape get_component, export_library and write_schlib use; a list with no entries and an optional field with no value are omitted rather than empty/null. For large libraries, use component_name to fetch specific symbols, or use limit/offset for pagination.

component_name.description: Optional: fetch only this symbol, by name in any case; a name the library does not hold is an error naming the available symbols

filepath.description: Path to the .SchLib file

limit.description: Optional: maximum number of symbols to return, 1 or more (default: all)

offset.description: Optional: skip the first N symbols, 0 or more (default: 0)

tools.name: list_components
tools.title: List components
tools.description: List all component/footprint names in an Altium library file (.PcbLib or .SchLib). Supports pagination with limit/offset for large libraries. Use include_metadata for additional details like part_count and pin_count.

filepath.description: Path to the library file

include_metadata.description: If true, return objects with metadata instead of just names: a footprint's description, one count per primitive kind and has_3d_model; a symbol's description, designator, part_count, pin_count and footprint_count. Default: false

limit.description: Maximum number of components to return, 1 or more (optional, default: all)

offset.description: Number of components to skip, 0 or more (optional, default: 0)

tools.name: extract_style
tools.title: Extract a library's style
tools.description: Extract style information from an existing Altium library file. A PcbLib reports track and arc widths per layer, pad shapes, text heights and the layer usage of every primitive kind (a via counts as Multi-Layer); a SchLib reports pin lengths, stroke widths and the stroke, fill and text colours of every record kind. Use this to learn from existing libraries and create consistent new components.

filepath.description: Path to the .PcbLib or .SchLib file

tools.name: write_pcblib
tools.title: Write a PcbLib
tools.description: Write footprints to an Altium .PcbLib file (set 'append': true to add to an existing library instead of replacing it). Each footprint is defined by its primitives: pads (with position, size, shape, layer), tracks, vias, fills, arcs, regions, text and component_bodies. The AI is responsible for calculating correct positions and sizes based on IPC-7351B or other standards. All coordinates and dimensions must be in millimetres (mm). A footprint authored without a '.Designator' text receives one on the Top Overlay automatically, just above its topmost pad, so every placed part shows its reference designator: supply your own to control its placement, or set 'auto_designator': false to omit it; a footprint echoed back from a read (carrying primitive_order) is never touched. The response 'bodies' array echoes each footprint's 3D body height and source; a footprint with no STEP model and no component body reports source 'none'. Set 'auto_3d_body': true to have an extruded placeholder body (default height 1.0 mm, flagged 'assumed_height': true) added to such footprints, then confirm or override it by supplying 'component_bodies' explicitly. The response also includes a 'warnings' array flagging silkscreen (overlay) tracks that overlap a pad (silk-on-pad) so you can move them clear. No text field may contain '|', the separator of Altium's record format, which cannot hold it.

append.description: If true, append to existing file; if false, create new file

auto_3d_body.description: If true, footprints with pads but no STEP model and no component body get a placeholder extruded 3D body (1.0 mm tall, flagged assumed_height). Default false: nothing is added unless you ask, since many footprints (fiducials, test points, mounting holes) legitimately have no body. Prefer supplying real heights via component_bodies.

auto_designator.description: If true (default), a footprint authored without a '.Designator' text gets one on the Top Overlay just above its topmost pad, so the placed part shows its reference designator. Never applied to a footprint echoed back from read_pcblib/get_component (one carrying primitive_order): Altium's own library footprints carry no designator text, and a read-modify-write must not add primitives. Set false to author a footprint without one.

Default: none

Pass it back unchanged so a read-modify-write keeps the identity Altium tracks for ECO; omit when authoring (a from-scratch primitive records none).

tools.title: Write a SchLib
tools.description: Write schematic symbols to an Altium .SchLib file (set 'append': true to add to an existing library instead of replacing it). Each symbol is defined by its primitives: pins, rectangles, round_rects, lines, polylines, polygons, arcs, pies, images, text_frames, beziers, ellipses, elliptical_arcs, labels, and text — plus its designator, parameters (Value, Manufacturer, ...) and footprint links ('footprints', name + optional library_path). Multi-part symbols set 'part_count' and tag each pin with 'owner_part_id'. Coordinates must be in schematic units (10 units = 1 grid square, not mm); a pin's (x, y) is its body-attach end and 'orientation' is the direction it points outward — the response echoes each pin's computed body_end and tip. No text field may contain '|', the separator of Altium's record format; Altium's own editor stores it as '¦' (U+00A6).

tools.name: search_components
tools.title: Search components
tools.description: Search for components across multiple Altium libraries using regex or glob patterns. Returns matching component names with their source library paths. Supports both `.PcbLib` (footprints) and `.SchLib` (symbols) files.

filepaths.description: Array of library file paths to search (.PcbLib or .SchLib)

pattern.description: Search pattern to match component names

pattern_type.description: Pattern type: 'glob' (wildcards like * and ?) or 'regex' (regular expressions). Default: 'glob'

tools.name: get_component
tools.title: Get a component
tools.description: Get a single component by name from an Altium library. Returns the full component data (footprint or symbol) without needing to read and filter the entire library. Supports both `.PcbLib` (footprints) and `.SchLib` (symbols) files.

component_name.description: Exact name of the component to retrieve

filepath.description: Path to the Altium library file (.PcbLib or .SchLib)

tools.name: component_exists
tools.title: Check components exist
tools.description: Check if one or more components exist in an Altium library. Use this to validate component names before operations like rename, copy, or delete. Supports both `.PcbLib` and `.SchLib` files.

component_names.description: List of component names to check

filepath.description: Path to the Altium library file (.PcbLib or .SchLib)

tools.name: render_footprint
tools.title: Preview a footprint
tools.description: Render an ASCII art visualisation of a footprint from a PcbLib file: every primitive kind — pads (with designators), vias, tracks, arcs, fills, regions, text marks and 3D-body outlines — each with its own marker, plus a per-kind count line and a legend. A quick preview, not a rendering.

component_name.description: Name of the footprint to render

filepath.description: Path to the Altium PcbLib file

scale.description: Characters per mm (default: 2.0). Higher = more detail

tools.name: render_symbol
tools.title: Preview a symbol
tools.description: Render an ASCII art visualisation of a schematic symbol from a SchLib file: every record kind of the requested part — pins (with designators), rectangles, rounded rectangles, lines, polylines, polygons, arcs, pies, ellipses, elliptical arcs, beziers, images, text frames, labels and IEEE symbols — each with its own marker, plus a per-kind count line and a legend. Coordinates are in schematic units (10 units = 1 grid).

component_name.description: Name of the symbol to render

filepath.description: Path to the Altium SchLib file

part_id.description: Part ID for multi-part symbols (default: 1, shows all parts if 0)

scale.description: Characters per 10 schematic units (default: 1.0). Higher = more detail

tools.name: manage_schlib_parameters
tools.title: Manage symbol parameters

filepath.description: Path to the Altium SchLib file

hidden.description: Whether the parameter is hidden (optional for set, add)

operation.description: Operation to perform: list (all parameters), get (single parameter), set (update value), add (new parameter), delete (remove parameter)

param_type.description: Parameter type (0=String, 1=Boolean, 2=Integer, 3=Float) (optional for set, add). Default: 0

parameter_name.description: Name of the parameter (required for get, set, add, delete); matched without regard to case, as Altium treats parameter names

read_only_state.description: Read-only state (0=editable, 1=read-only) (optional for set, add). Default: 0

unique_id.description: 8-char Altium unique ID (optional for set, add). Default: auto-generated

x.description: X position in schematic units (optional for set, add)

y.description: Y position in schematic units (optional for set, add)

tools.name: manage_schlib_footprints
tools.title: Manage symbol footprint links
tools.description: Manage footprint links in Altium SchLib symbols. Supports listing, adding, and removing footprint references that link schematic symbols to PCB footprints.

component_name.description: Name of the symbol to manage footprints for

description.description: Footprint description (optional for add). Keep to 256 characters if the library will be imported into an Altium 365 workspace — that importer refuses longer ones; a longer description is written and reported as a validation warning.

filepath.description: Path to the Altium SchLib file

library_path.description: Optional (add): absolute path to the .PcbLib containing the footprint, written as ModelDatafile0 so Altium can resolve and preview the model. Omit to link by name only (requires the library to be installed/in the project, else 'footprint not found').

operation.description: Operation to perform: list (all footprints), add (new footprint link), remove (delete footprint link)

tools.name: compare_components
tools.title: Compare two components
tools.description: Compare two specific components in detail, showing differences in primitives, parameters, and properties. Components can be from the same library or different libraries. Returns primitive-level differences for every kind: pads, vias, tracks, arcs, regions, text, fills and 3D bodies of a footprint; pins, every graphic shape, parameters and footprint links of a symbol. Identity (GUIDs, unique ids) is never a difference.

filepath_a.description: Path to the first library file (.PcbLib or .SchLib)

filepath_b.description: Path to the second library file (can be same as filepath_a)

include_geometry.description: Include detailed geometry comparisons for primitives (default: true)

tolerance.description: Tolerance for floating-point comparisons in mm (default: 0.001)

tools.name: repair_library
tools.title: Repair a library
tools.description: Repair a PcbLib by removing orphaned 3D-model data: (1) embedded models not referenced by any footprint, and (2) component body references that point to non-existent models. This fixes libraries where STEP model data is missing but references remain (validate_library reports both conditions). PcbLib only; a SchLib is refused.

dry_run.description: If true, report what would be fixed without making changes (default: false)

filepath.description: Path to the library file (.PcbLib)

tools.name: list_backups
tools.title: List backups
tools.description: List available backup files for an Altium library. Shows timestamped .bak files that were automatically created before write operations.

filepath.description: Path to the library file (.PcbLib or .SchLib)

tools.name: restore_backup
tools.title: Restore a backup
tools.description: Restore an Altium library file from a backup. If no specific backup is specified, restores from the most recent backup. The current file is snapshotted as a new backup first (reported as pre_restore_backup), so a wrong pick is itself reversible, and the restore is written atomically.

backup_path.description: Optional: specific backup file to restore from. If not provided, uses most recent backup.

filepath.description: Path to the library file to restore

tools.name: bulk_rename
tools.title: Rename components by pattern
tools.description: Rename multiple components in a library using regex pattern matching. Supports capture groups for flexible renaming (e.g., 'RESC(.*)' -> 'RES_$1').

dry_run.description: If true, show what would be renamed without making changes (default: false)

filepath.description: Path to the library file (.PcbLib or .SchLib)

pattern.description: Regex pattern to match component names (e.g., '^RESC(.*)$')

replacement.description: Replacement string with optional capture groups (e.g., 'RES_$1')

tools.name: update_pad
tools.title: Update a pad
tools.description: Update specific properties of a pad in a PcbLib footprint without replacing the entire component. Find pad by designator and apply only the specified updates. On a stacked pad (stack_mode other than simple) a width/height/shape change also reaches the per-layer tables: layers that shared the old primary value follow it, layers with their own value keep it, and the response reports how many followed.

component_name.description: Name of the footprint containing the pad

dry_run.description: If true, show what would change without saving (default: false)

filepath.description: Path to the .PcbLib file

updates.description: Properties to update (only specified properties are changed)

hole_size.description: New hole diameter for through-hole pads

shape.description: New pad shape. Same vocabulary as write_pcblib: rectangle, rounded_rectangle, round/circle, oval, octagonal. Matching is case-insensitive and ignores '_'/'-'.

tools.name: update_primitive
tools.title: Update a primitive
tools.description: Update specific properties of a primitive (track, arc, text, fill, region or via) in a PcbLib footprint. Find the primitive by type and index (its position in read_pcblib's list for that type), apply only the specified updates. Moving a primitive to another layer drops the layer carriers it was read with (a region's v7_layer, an unmapped raw_layer_id) so the new layer's own token is written. On a stacked via (diameter_stack_mode other than simple) a diameter change also reaches per_layer_diameters: layers that shared the old diameter follow it, layers with their own value keep it, and the response reports how many followed.

component_name.description: Name of the footprint containing the primitive

dry_run.description: If true, show what would change without saving (default: false)

filepath.description: Path to the .PcbLib file

index.description: Zero-based index of the primitive within its type array

primitive_type.description: Type of primitive to update. Addressed by `index` into that primitive list. Pads are not here — they have a designator, so use update_pad.

updates.description: Properties to update (only specified properties are changed). Valid properties depend on primitive_type — track: x1, y1, x2, y2, width, layer; arc: x/x1, y/y1, radius, start_angle, end_angle, width, layer; text: x, y, height, rotation, text, layer; fill: x/x1, y/y1, x2, y2, rotation, layer; region: layer; via: x, y, diameter, hole_size, from_layer, to_layer. Any other key is refused.

layer.description: Layer name (track, arc, text, fill, region)
